narrator.name: Joseph Jacks
narrator.role: Founder and General Partner, OSS Capital; co-founder and CEO, Latent Holdings
narrator.one_line: Commercial open source investor who bought TAO in early 2023, committed a dedicated $25M in January 2024, then became a builder through Latent Holdings (subnets 14 and 5) and co-hosted The TAO Pod, framing Bittensor as Bitcoin and Linux applied to AI and as a transformation of capitalism itself.

statements.quote: The AI founder I'm most inspired by ... over the last year is Jake Steeves (@const_reborn), father of Bittensor. ... Instead of easily joining or founding a closed and heavily VC-funded foundation model startup, Jake decided to commit to a different path… one that would change the course of his life and, over time, everyone else's forever.
statements.context: Opening of his first long blog post on Bittensor, posted the same day as a thread on X, introducing Jacob Steeves to his open source audience.

source.title: Bittensor and $TAO

statements.quote: a type of specialized blockchain engineered to scalably train and run AI models of all kinds, sizes, levels of sophistication and purpose… without censorship… without discrimination… and one of the fundamental aspects of this system would lie in how it incentivizes the production of better and better intelligences for the benefit of all species
statements.context: Describing what Steeves conceived in 2016, in the same blog post.

source.title: Bittensor and $TAO

statements.quote: A handful of very early believers like @BarrySilbert and some others invested in the project at the very early stages of its development — I personally invested in early 2023.
statements.context: Placing himself in the investor lineage of the project, in the same blog post.

source.title: Bittensor and $TAO

statements.quote: the mission they are on is deeply profound … create robust and incorruptible systems that enable open source and permissionless AI (and AGI + ASI + whatever other goal-post-moving acronyms materialize from here) in a way that truly does ensure equal opportunity and access to the best intelligences possible in all domains.
statements.context: Stating the mission as he reads it, in the same blog post.

source.title: Bittensor and $TAO

statements.quote: This last year brought on high levels of awareness and participation across a broad set of stakeholders, miners, developers, end users, speculators, analysts and researchers all working toward the same mission: make AI a sustainable common good.
statements.context: Naming the audiences of the network and the one line mission, in the X version of the post.

source.title: The AI founder I'm most inspired by

statements.quote: I'm extremely excited about the future of this project and this is absolutely not investment advice, but you should go out and figure out how to acquire some $TAO. Then do yourself a favor and hold it forever.
statements.context: Closing line of the X thread, addressed to his followers.

source.title: The AI founder I'm most inspired by

statements.quote: OSS Capital is committing $25M to invest exclusively in the Bittensor ecosystem. We believe Bittensor represents the most vibrant community and network focused on accelerating decentralized and truly open AI for all.
statements.context: Announcement post on his blog and LinkedIn of a dedicated OSS Capital allocation to Bittensor.

source.title: $25 Million Commitment to Bittensor

statements.quote: Bittensor is generating > $150M in revenue compensation for developers building AI services on the network. Growing exponentially. As a VC funded startup, it would be valued at > $15 Billion. Instead, it's a decentralized cap table for all. Trading at $2B~. Let it be known.
statements.context: Post on X comparing the network's emission spend with how a venture backed startup would be valued.

source.title: Bittensor is generating > $150M in revenue

statements.quote: 7,200 Bittensor $TAO tokens get emitted to the network every day until the first halving in September 2025. That's $4 million per day, $120 million per month and $1.5 billion annually. ... A whopping THIRD of these teams are earning millions of dollars every month… and the bar is still low given the nascency of Bittensor. Jump in. You're welcome.
statements.context: LinkedIn post pointing developers at the emission budget and the size of subnet teams.

source.title: 7,200 Bittensor $TAO tokens get emitted to the network every day

statements.quote: Bittensor was envisioned and founded before OpenAI.
statements.context: Quote post of a Jacob Steeves tweet, asserting the network's priority over the closed lab.

source.title: Bittensor was envisioned and founded before OpenAI

statements.quote: The number (15+) of Bittensor-dedicated startups is growing exponentially 📈 … ! How many Bittensor competitors can remotely boast the same? Zero.
statements.context: Post on X listing fifteen subnet and tooling teams as evidence of ecosystem growth.

source.title: The number (15+) of Bittensor-dedicated startups is growing exponentially

statements.quote: Pack it up folks. Bittensor is a scam. Looks too much like Bitcoin. 😬
statements.context: Sarcastic quote post replying to @defi_mochi, who had argued that half of circulating supply would hit the market within a year.

source.title: Pack it up folks. Bittensor is a scam.

statements.quote: We invest in open source startups exclusively. We're not really a crypto or Web 3 or like blockchain investor.
statements.context: Answering Laura Shin's opening question about what OSS Capital is, on Unchained with Sami Kassab.

source.title: Could Bittensor End Up Being the Only Crypto/AI Project That Matters? (Ep. 712)

statements.quote: I learned about BitTensor early last year, January, February timeframe. And initially was very skeptical of BitTenser, I think, as most kind of non-crypto, non-blockchain native people tend to be
statements.context: Asked on Unchained how OSS Capital came to the project; wording as rendered by the auto transcript.

source.title: Could Bittensor End Up Being the Only Crypto/AI Project That Matters? (Ep. 712)

statements.quote: And so we actually think there's going to be a huge shift from the centralized AI, proprietary AI kind of closed companies to BitTensor really incentivizing this large commodity marketplace.
statements.context: Explaining the investment thesis on Unchained.

source.title: Could Bittensor End Up Being the Only Crypto/AI Project That Matters? (Ep. 712)

statements.quote: I think BitTensor is really, for the first time, kind of like putting a stake in the ground and saying, we should apply these same types of principles, Bitcoin with fiat currencies, Linux, with closed proprietary operating systems.
statements.context: On Unchained, drawing the precedent of Bitcoin and Linux for what Bittensor does to AI.

source.title: Could Bittensor End Up Being the Only Crypto/AI Project That Matters? (Ep. 712)

statements.quote: You should not have to go and get a job at one of these big tech companies. You should not have to go and raise capital from a VC...you should not have to go and get someone's sign off and okay.
statements.context: On Unchained, describing what permissionless participation means for a builder.

source.title: Could Bittensor End Up Being the Only Crypto/AI Project That Matters? (Ep. 712)

statements.quote: What BitTensor is actually doing is inverting capitalism...get rewarded by this token, which is increasingly worth more as you have more activity contribution on the network...you're only producing open commodities.
statements.context: On Unchained, contrasting the network's model with a venture funded AI company.

source.title: Could Bittensor End Up Being the Only Crypto/AI Project That Matters? (Ep. 712)

statements.quote: I personally believe that all of these kind of fear-mongering concerns...are completely baseless...technology is amoral and apolitical...Where the risk comes from is how humans apply the technology.
statements.context: On Unchained, asked whether AI poses dangers to humanity.

source.title: Could Bittensor End Up Being the Only Crypto/AI Project That Matters? (Ep. 712)

statements.quote: they really want to do what's called regulatory capture...this is the most powerful and interesting kind of development that humans have ever kind of discovered...It's never been more important to create a platform...democratically.
statements.context: On Unchained, on what the large AI labs want from regulators and why that argues for an open platform.

source.title: Could Bittensor End Up Being the Only Crypto/AI Project That Matters? (Ep. 712)

statements.quote: From first principles about the amount of capital and talent that you could aggregate in a decentralized permissionless system, it vastly vastly outstrips all of the big internet companies combined.
statements.context: Closing argument on Unchained for why the network can compete with the largest AI companies.

source.title: Could Bittensor End Up Being the Only Crypto/AI Project That Matters? (Ep. 712)

statements.quote: I own no Bitcoin, my only massive exposure to a proof-of-useful-work token is Bittensor $TAO which will get to $100K in 1/2 the time it took $BTC. But this is a happy day. Am immensely important milestone. Bitcoin is the MOTHER of Bittensor.
statements.context: Post on X on the day Bitcoin first crossed $100,000.

source.title: Bitcoin is the MOTHER of Bittensor

statements.quote: Bittensor is showing us what the potentially perfect form of direct democracy (dd) could look like. ... My prediction is that Bittensor dTAO (dynamic TAO) will be the most interesting and potentially successful form of dd in human history.
statements.context: Thread on X pushing back on Marc Andreessen's dismissal of direct democracy on the Lex Fridman podcast, weeks before dTAO went live.

source.title: Bittensor is showing us what the potentially perfect form of direct democracy could look like

statements.quote: But instead of a single commodity on the network like SHA256 Hashes on Bitcoin, there's N commodities … ! Each commodity takes a slice of the network to express its "incentive mechanism" ..which is basically an arbitrarily complex program that specifies the boot-loader logic for a loss function that optimizes over a problem space.
statements.context: Same thread, explaining subnets to a general audience.

source.title: Bittensor is showing us what the potentially perfect form of direct democracy could look like

statements.quote: Bittensor $TAO is the only borderless incentive layer for accelerating the continuously improving production of open source AI on many dimensions. This layer has already surpassed critical mass adoption by builders. It still lags cutting edge centralized open source efforts — but it will surpass those over the coming years just as open always does with closed when properly applied.
statements.context: Long post on X a few days before the dTAO upgrade, restating his thesis.

source.title: Bittensor $TAO is the only borderless incentive layer

statements.quote: Bittensor uses the exact same architectural principles to enable anyone to express an incentive mechanism and unlock latent talent toward a common objective function: proof of useful utility work, directly undergirding the applications that are redefining the future of computing.
statements.context: Same post, after comparing Bittensor's design with Bitcoin's SHA-256 commodity production.

source.title: Bittensor $TAO is the only borderless incentive layer

statements.quote: By example, on the first few moments of the dTAO merge a few hours ago, many subnets were trading at $10-20 billion FDVs… bringing the "total synthetic" FDV of Bittensor itself to well over $100B.
statements.context: Post on X hours after dynamic TAO went live, explaining alpha token supply and valuation.

source.title: Alpha tokens on Bittensor have 21m finite supply

statements.quote: I have changed my mind about Bittensor subnet owner teams mining their own network. They should. If the incentive mechanism is rigorously well designed to produce an infinitely improving commodity - and heavily resistant to exploitation.
statements.context: Post on X reversing an earlier position on subnet owners mining their own subnets, addressed to subnet teams.

source.title: I have changed my mind about Bittensor subnet owner teams mining their own network

statements.quote: Focus on the beauty and fundamental advantage of Bittensor: Permissionless extrinsic ($TAO and corresponding alpha) incentives for producing continuously improving N dimensional digital commodities. The entire point is to create a sustainable "bootstrapped" activation energy for teams anywhere to create asymmetrical contributions without the need to get ANYONE's permission for anything... especially a VC.
statements.context: Same post, advising subnet teams against raising venture capital.

source.title: I have changed my mind about Bittensor subnet owner teams mining their own network

foundation.mission.summary: Bittensor exists to incentivize the production of ever better, open, permissionless intelligence that anyone can access, with AI as a sustainable common good rather than a closed product.

foundation.vision.summary: He sees subnets as merit-based market networks that replace networks run by kings, corporations and mobs, a workable direct democracy with capitalism embedded, and a system whose incentives will tighten toward mathematical precision over time.

foundation.values.summary: Permissionless participation without a job at big tech, a VC or anyone's sign off; equal access; technology treated as amoral, with the risk located in human application.

problem.cultural.summary: AI fear-mongering is baseless in his telling; the real danger is how humans and institutions apply the technology.

problem.market.summary: The network's builders outperform venture funded rivals but fail to engage the conventional research world, so the world does not know.

problem.institutional.summary: Large labs seek regulatory capture over the most powerful technology humans have discovered, which makes a democratically built platform urgent.

opportunity.summary: A permissionless system can aggregate more capital and talent than all big internet companies combined; emission budgets, halvings and subnet revenue are cited as tailwinds.

audience.summary: He talks to developers and subnet teams (jump in, mine your own subnet, do not raise VC) and to holders (acquire TAO and hold it forever).

positioning.category.summary: Bittensor is Bitcoin and Linux applied to AI: a commodity marketplace, an incentive layer, a form of direct democracy, and a transformation of capitalism the way Bitcoin transformed capital.

positioning.differentiator.summary: N commodities instead of one, permissionless extrinsic incentives, no venture funding and a fairer ownership distribution than early Bitcoin; it inverts the AI business model by rewarding open outputs.

positioning.reason.summary: Open beat closed before (Linux, Bitcoin), the community is full of builders, and OSS Capital has committed its own capital for ten plus years.

positioning.against.summary: Set against closed, VC-funded foundation model startups and OpenAI (which the network predates), against VC-funded imitators with pre-mine sales and no mainnet, against critics of emissions, and against regulatory capture by big labs.

value.functional.summary: Builders get paid in TAO and alpha for useful work without permission, a job, or a fundraise; subnets let merit govern without a ruler.

messaging.h1.summary: The repeated line moves from 'make AI a sustainable common good' to 'the only borderless incentive layer' to the aphorism 'Bitcoin transforms capital. Bittensor transforms capitalism.'

messaging.proof.summary: Emission spend in dollars, counts of dedicated startups, subnet valuations versus startup comps (Chutes, Ridges), founder ownership under one percent, and zero venture dollars raised.

voice.summary: Sarcastic toward critics, profane when rallying, willing to reverse himself in public and to call the network lossy and bad at outreach.

relationship.summary: An open source investor, not a crypto investor, who bought early in 2023 after initial skepticism, committed a dedicated fund, then became a builder and steward through Latent Holdings and an advisor to a TAO treasury company.

language.term.summary: He coins investor-flavored terms: decentralized cap table, proof of useful utility work, synthetic FDV, stocks for ideas, incentives as a meta language, and describes incentive mechanisms as boot-loader logic for a loss function.

AGI as a serious term (goal-post-moving acronyms)

genealogy.summary: Jacks goes public in January 2024 with a founder tribute and a $25M commitment, framing Bittensor through Steeves' refusal of the closed, VC-funded path and the mission to make AI a sustainable common good [joseph-jacks-001] [joseph-jacks-007] [joseph-jacks-005]. On Unchained he sets the precedent as Bitcoin plus Linux and says the network is inverting capitalism [joseph-jacks-016] [joseph-jacks-018], and his proof is dollars: emission spend, startup counts, startup comps [joseph-jacks-008] [joseph-jacks-011]. By late January 2025 he is previewing dTAO as direct democracy [joseph-jacks-023].

After the upgrade he speaks as a builder as much as an investor: Latent Holdings launches TAOHash on subnet 14 and he advises subnet teams to mine their own networks and refuse VC money [joseph-jacks-031] [joseph-jacks-028] [joseph-jacks-029]. The capitalism line hardens into an aphorism [joseph-jacks-033] [joseph-jacks-035], subnets become stocks for ideas and market networks replacing rulers [joseph-jacks-038] [joseph-jacks-041], VC-funded imitators become the foil [joseph-jacks-043], and he turns critical of the network's own outreach and precision [joseph-jacks-036] [joseph-jacks-045].
genealogy.shift: From investor advocacy built on precedent and dollar proof to builder and steward voice, with the Bitcoin comparison compressed into slogans and new self-criticism.

genealogy.summary: No Bittensor statements from June 2026 onward were reached. His last found Bittensor item is a January 2026 LinkedIn tribute to Steeves [joseph-jacks-048]; his April 2026 post on Anthropic's Mythos argues for open weights without naming Bittensor, and the TAO Pod's August 2026 relaunch says he is no longer a co-host.
genealogy.shift: Public Bittensor output thins; whether this is a step back or a search gap is unresolved.
